 The German Patriot Office annually helps the local community remember when the wall came tumbling down.
 The Berlin Wall fell on Nov. 9, 1989, ending the 45-year post-World War II division of their native land into East Germany (German Democratic Republic) and West Germany (Federal Republic of Germany).
 German Unity Day is celebrated every year as Germany’s national holiday, marking the official reunification of the country in 1990.
 “It is to commemorate, to celebrate, the German reunification,” German Air Force Lt. Col. Markus Koeppen, director of the German Patriot Office, said while welcoming guests at the door of their celebration event Oct. 19 in the Bicentennial Chapel fellowship hall. “That was in 1990.”
 An estimated 70 people attended the celebration, which included a buffet lunch, cake cutting and remarks.
 Birmingham resident Tine Hoffmeister, executive director of the Alabama Germany Partnership, shared her thoughts about German Unity Day.
 “Today we celebrate the triumph of unity over division,” she said.
 Pam Stieglitz of Hampton Cove was among the attendees. “I enjoy so much our German friends,” she said, “and look forward to seeing them.”
